advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Do not call record_sweep() when run_sweep stands aside for a busy store lock (stamp only when a sweep actually ran).
evidence: docstring at :278-280 states the staleness arm is 'what makes this a real floor rather than a coincidence' — resetting the stamp on a no-fold stand-aside undermines that floor
advisory.finding: run_sweep() stamps the sweep in its finally block even when it stood aside because the store write lock was busy (write_lock_is_busy() true → early return → finally runs record_sweep). A stand-aside performs no fold yet resets the last-sweep stamp, so on a store under sustained foreground write contention every close's worker stands aside and refreshes the stamp, keeping the staleness arm from ever firing — compaction can be deferred indefinitely, which is exactly the 'floor' the staleness arm exists to guarantee.
scenarios: A busy store where a foreground writer is active every time a close's detached worker probes: each worker stands aside, stamps the sweep fresh, and the staleness arm never fires, so foldable tickets accumulate unbounded.
advisory.suggested_fix: Stamp the sweep only on the path that actually ran compact_all_cli — e.g. move record_sweep out of the unconditional finally, or skip it on the write_lock_is_busy early return, so a stand-aside does not reset the staleness clock.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consolidate sweep stamping to a single owning call site rather than stamping in both compact_all_cli and run_sweep.finally.
evidence: run_sweep at :266-267 calls `_compact.compact_all_cli([], repo_root=repo_root)` which itself stamps
advisory.finding: record_sweep(tracker) runs twice for every successful detached/inline sweep: once inside compact_all_cli() (compact.py:427-430) and again in run_sweep()'s finally (compact_trigger.py:271). Redundant filesystem writes and a subtle coupling — the finally-stamp is what the stand-aside path relies on, so the two call sites are not obviously separable.
scenarios: Any successful sweep via run_sweep writes the stamp twice.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the transition_close.py:503-517 comment to reflect that the close now TRIGGERS (without performing) compaction via _trigger_compaction.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:503: `# Compaction is NOT run here (bug choosy-arthrodic-barbet). It used to be...`
src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:515-517: `... the standing trigger is now an` / `out-of-band sweep that runs in a DEDICATED CLONE...`
advisory.finding: The pre-existing explanatory comment in close_ticket (transition_close.py:503-517) still asserts 'Compaction is NOT run here' and frames the standing trigger as 'now an out-of-band sweep that runs in a DEDICATED CLONE', but the new `_trigger_compaction(...)` call at line 529 reintroduces an operation-linked trigger directly below it. The comment now contradicts the code a few lines down and will mislead a future reader about the close's behavior.
scenarios: A maintainer reads the block at 503-517 and concludes the close never triggers compaction, missing the trigger added at 529.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting compact_all_cli writes the sweep stamp on a real run and leaves it unchanged on a --dry-run.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:427 `if not dry_run:` guarding `compact_trigger.record_sweep(tracker)` with comment 'A dry run stamps nothing — it did not sweep.'

search of tests/ for `compact-sweep.stamp` returns (no matches); `_sweep_stamp_path` appears only in test_compact_trigger.py:161 (staleness arm), never asserting the dry-run-vs-real stamping branch introduced in compact.py
ABSENCE: no test drives compact_all_cli with and without --dry-run and inspects whether the sweep stamp mtime changed
advisory.finding: The new dry-run guard on the sweep stamp in compact.py ('A dry run stamps nothing') is untested: no test asserts that `compact_all_cli(['--dry-run'...])` leaves the compact-sweep stamp unwritten while a real sweep writes it. A regression that stamped on a dry run (or failed to stamp on a real sweep) would age the staleness floor without folding, defeating the very floor the change adds, and nothing would catch it.
scenarios: A future edit drops the `not dry_run` guard, so scheduled/inline dry runs stamp the sweep and suppress the staleness trigger even though no fold occurred — the CI-less floor silently stops working, undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_compact_all_selection.py, add: capture the stamp mtime (or its absence) via compact_trigger._sweep_stamp_path; assert a --dry-run compact_all_cli does NOT create/update it, and a real compact_all_cli DOES.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture rebar's own exit code independent of the tee pipeline (e.g. `rebar compact-all "${ARGS[@]}" > >(tee "${RUNNER_TEMP}/sweep.out") ; rc=$?` or use `PIPESTATUS[0]`) so a tee failure cannot mask or override the fold exit code.
evidence: `set -euo pipefail` at line 143 enables pipefail for this step

Comment at lines 147-149 states the contract: "Exit 2 means some tickets errored ... surface it without failing the run. A real invocation error (exit 1) still fails." — this contract now keys off the pipeline status, not rebar's status.
advisory.finding: Adding `| tee "${RUNNER_TEMP}/sweep.out"` under `set -o pipefail` makes the captured `rc` the pipeline's rightmost non-zero exit, so a `tee` write failure (e.g. non-writable RUNNER_TEMP or full disk) masks rebar's real exit code and can fail an otherwise-successful best-effort sweep — or hide the exit-2 vs exit-1 distinction the workflow explicitly branches on.
scenarios: RUNNER_TEMP is unwritable or the runner disk fills; tee exits non-zero while rebar exited 0 or 2, so rc reflects tee and the run either fails spuriously or misreports the fold outcome.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `set +o pipefail` locally around the pipe, or read `rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}` immediately after the pipeline, so the branch decision uses rebar's exit code rather than the pipeline's.
